questions.a: Restaurant marketing is how you show the public what makes your restaurant different and build a connection with guests. It covers everything from your brand identity and website to social media, reviews, email and loyalty programs. The goal is to bring in new guests and keep existing ones coming back.

questions.q: How do I create a marketing strategy for my restaurant?
questions.a: Start by defining your goals, your unique selling points, your budget and the kinds of guests you want to reach. From there, build a clear brand identity and choose the channels that fit, such as social media, your website, email and SMS. Review what's working regularly and adjust as you learn.

questions.q: What are the best digital marketing channels for restaurants?
questions.a: Social media, your Google Business Profile, online reviews, email and SMS are the core digital channels for most restaurants. Your website matters too, since many diners check it before visiting or ordering. Paid social ads can help you reach new audiences, especially when you target them using your own customer data.

questions.q: Are loyalty programs worth it for a restaurant?
questions.a: Yes, keeping loyal guests usually costs far less than finding new ones, so a loyalty program is often a smart investment. The best programs are easy to join, work online and in store, and reward members with exclusive offers. They also give you a reason to stay in touch through email and text messages.

questions.q: How does guest feedback help restaurant marketing?
questions.a: Reviews and feedback show you what guests value about your restaurant, which helps you sharpen your message. Analyzing sentiment across reviews and surveys reveals the dishes and moments people talk about most. You can then build campaigns around what's already resonating with your guests.
